simple.meaning: זְמוֹרָה (zᵉmôwrâh) is a Hebrew object word meaning “a twig (as pruned ).” BibleIQ follows the concrete thing through the verses where it appears.
simple.biblicalBackground: The occurrence trail begins at Numbers 13:23. The surrounding context includes family line, land.
simple.inThisVerse: In this verse, the tapped English word is source-aligned to זְמוֹרָה (H2156) in the Hebrew text.
simple.whyItMatters: Concrete words often carry patterns through Scripture because objects, animals, offerings, and created things are used repeatedly in worship, judgment, covenant, and narrative.
simple.summary: זְמוֹרָה (zᵉmôwrâh) / H2156 is traced through Numbers 13:23, Isaiah 17:10, Ezekiel 8:17, Ezekiel 15:2 with generated occurrence evidence.

definitions.full: H2156. zemorah זְמוֺרָה noun [feminine] branch, twig, shoot — absolute ׳ז Num 13:23 , ׳הַזּ Ezek 8:17 ; 15:2 ; construct זְמֹרַת Isa 17:10 ; suffix זְמֹרֵיהֶם Nahum 2:3 ; — branch of grape-vine Num 13:23 (JE), Ezek 15:2 ; branch, twig (Co Reissigbündel ) used in idolatrous worship ׳הַזּ אֶלאַֿמָּם 8:17 (see Sm and most), but custom obscure (see Da), and text dubious; זָר זְמֹרַת (compare Ew § 287 b ) Isa 17:10 twigs of a strange one (i.e. of a strange god) figurative of idolatrous cults adopted by Israel; ׳ז plural in figure of Israelites Nahum 2:3 .
